newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian industry seen growing at 8 to 9 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Indian industry seen growing at 8 to 9 pct in 1997.

text.p: Indian industrial growth will pick up by October and grow an average of eight or nine percent through 1996 and into 1997, investment banker Crosby Securities said in an economic review on Wednesday.
"We expect industrial growth to pick up by October," Crosby said in its latest South Asia Economic Review.
"By then, the easy liquidity conditions that prevailed in recent months will reverse the impact of the late 1995 liquidity crunch which initially caused the industrial slowdown," it said.
Industrial growth had declined to 7.7 percent year on year in April from 9.6 percent in March and 13.1 percent in February. Almost all sectors of the economy were affected, Crosby said.

It said good monsoon rains during June-August 1996 will continue to feed rural consumption demand, ensure plentiful supply of industrial raw materials such as raw cotton and jute and support hydroelectric power generation.
"Since India has experienced exceptionally good monsoon rains during June-August, we expect rural prosperity to keep consumption demand strong," Crosby said.
"Overall, industrial growth will average 8-9 percent in 1996/97 (April-March) compared to 12 percent in 1995/96."
Electricity generation growth fell in recent months and is now significantly lower than overall rate of industrial expansion, the report said.

This is partly structural because of inadequate power generation capacity expansion. However, it is also the result of a sharp fall in hydroelectric power generation which normally accounts for 18-20 percent of total power output, it said.
"Provisional data suggests that May and June also experienced negative growth rates. However, this trend should now reverse since most reservoirs now have adequate water," the report said.
